- If sentiment is consistently neutral or absent, model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- When true price moves sharply upward, model frequently lags by 2–4 days; apply a 1–2 day lag correction with smoothing to align with actual trend.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., -1.00 or >0.20), model underestimates downward moves; increase forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–4% for next 5–7 days.
- In absence of sentiment, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% for 30-day horizon.
